title: Message Queues
subtitle: A queue turns 'do it now' into 'do it soon', and asks you to handle 'twice'
motto: Answer fast, work later, and expect duplicates
keyInsight: A queue keeps the request fast and absorbs bursts, but it only defers overload and, with at-least-once delivery, requires consumers that can safely see a message twice.

decisions.title: Show that the queue only hides a spike
decisions.description: The failure frame reports backlog and wait time, because the user-facing response stays fast while the work quietly falls behind.
decisions.alternatives: Reporting only response time would make a queue look like it solves overload.

decisions.title: Frame delivery as duplicates versus loss
decisions.description: The trade-off frame gives the same number of affected jobs either way, duplicated under at-least-once and lost under at-most-once, so the choice is clear.
decisions.alternatives: Explaining the three guarantees abstractly would not show why at-least-once with idempotent consumers is the default.
